questions.explain: Native vector support needs SQL Server 2025 (17.x); the chapter's first step is confirming the engine version before anything else.
options: Version 15, verified via SELECT @@VERSION only
Version 16, verified via the Windows registry
Version 17 — run SELECT SERVERPROPERTY('ProductMajorVersion') and expect 17, e.g. 'Microsoft SQL Server 2025 (RTM) - 17.0.xxxx'
Version 14 with a compatibility-level override
questions.q: SQL Server 2025 reports itself as which major version, and how do you verify it?

questions.explain: Design so the GA features carry the production load and the preview index is an accelerator you can adopt, drop, or rebuild without redesigning tables.
options: GA: VECTOR(n), VECTOR_DISTANCE (cosine/euclidean/dot), VECTOR_NORM, VECTOR_NORMALIZE; Preview: the DiskANN vector index (CREATE VECTOR INDEX) and the VECTOR_SEARCH table-valued function
GA: everything including DiskANN; Preview: nothing
GA: VECTOR_SEARCH; Preview: the VECTOR type itself
GA: only exact search up to 1,000 vectors; Preview: everything else
questions.q: Which vector features are generally available (production-ready) versus preview in SQL Server 2025?

questions.explain: Preview status carries real constraints; that is why the chapter says keep source documents in ordinary tables and add the index as a performance layer, not a structural dependency.
options: It requires a GPU on the database server
It only works on tables with fewer than 10,000 rows
It supports partitioned tables and views

The table needs a single-column integer clustered primary key, becomes read-only while the index exists, the index must be dropped and recreated to ingest new data, and partitioned tables/views/temp tables are unsupported
questions.q: Which is a real preview constraint of the DiskANN vector index in SQL Server 2025?

questions.explain: The strict CAST is a guardrail — it catches a model-configuration mistake before it poisons the index — and ModelName is recorded per row because vectors from different models live in different coordinate spaces.
options: To reduce storage by 50%
So that attempting to store a 384-dimension vector in a VECTOR(1536) column fails loudly at write time — silent dimension mismatches are a notorious source of garbage search results
Because all embedding models output exactly 1,536 dimensions
To enable automatic normalization
questions.q: In the chapter's canonical table pattern, why is the VECTOR(1536) dimension count fixed at the type level?

questions.explain: The VECTOR type is new to the TDS type system, so plan a driver upgrade alongside the engine upgrade (EF Core 10+ has built-in vector support).
options: The database engine crashes
Forgetting to create the DiskANN index
An old SqlClient or ODBC driver that cannot parse the new TDS type metadata for VECTOR columns — the driver is the first suspect when vector reads fail while everything else works
Insufficient disk space for the transaction log
